stories.headline: Anthropic Launches 'Dreaming' for Claude Managed Agents, Enabling Self-Improvement Between Sessions

key_facts.fact: Anthropic launched 'dreaming' as a research preview in Claude Managed Agents — a scheduled process that reviews past agent sessions and memory stores, extracts patterns, and curates memories so agents improve over time.
key_facts.excerpt: Dreaming is a scheduled process that reviews your agent sessions and memory stores, extracts patterns, and curates memories so your agents improve over time.

key_facts.fact: Dreaming surfaces patterns a single agent can't see, including recurring mistakes, workflows agents converge on, and team-wide preferences; users can choose automatic memory updates or review changes first.
key_facts.excerpt: Dreaming surfaces patterns that a single agent can't see on its own, including recurring mistakes, workflows that agents converge on, and preferences shared across a team. It also restructures memory so it stays high-signal as it evolves.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic also made 'outcomes' generally available — a feature where a rubric-based grader evaluates agent output in a separate context window and the agent self-corrects, improving task success by up to 10 points over standard prompting.
key_facts.excerpt: In testing, outcomes improved task success by up to 10 points over a standard prompting loop, with the largest gains on the hardest problems. Outcomes also improved file generation quality, with +8.4% task success on docx and +10.1% on pptx.

key_facts.fact: Multiagent orchestration was also made broadly available, allowing a lead agent to delegate subtasks to specialist agents with separate context windows and tools, while maintaining a shared memory store.
key_facts.excerpt: Today we're... making outcomes, multiagent orchestration, and webhooks available to developers building with Managed Agents. Together, these updates make agents more capable at handling complex tasks with minimal steering.

key_facts.fact: The features were announced at Anthropic's Code with Claude developer conference in San Francisco, where CEO Dario Amodei said the company could grow by 80x in 2026 and its growth rate is 'too hard to handle.'
key_facts.excerpt: The announcements were made as Anthropic held a developer day in San Francisco where it touted a new feature for its Claude AI, which it calls 'dreaming.'

stories.headline: Anthropic Signs Deal for All of SpaceX's Colossus 1 Capacity, Doubles Claude Code Rate Limits

key_facts.fact: Anthropic signed an agreement with SpaceX to use all of the compute capacity at the Colossus 1 data center in Memphis, gaining access to more than 300 MW of new capacity (over 220,000 NVIDIA GPUs including H100, H200, and GB200 accelerators) within the month.
key_facts.excerpt: We've signed an agreement with SpaceX to use all of the compute capacity at their Colossus 1 data center. This gives us access to more than 300 megawatts of new capacity (over 220,000 NVIDIA GPUs) within the month.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic doubled Claude Code's five-hour rate limits for Pro, Max, Team, and seat-based Enterprise plans, removed the peak hours limit reduction on Claude Code for Pro and Max accounts, and raised API rate limits considerably for Claude Opus models — all effective May 6.
key_facts.excerpt: First, we're doubling Claude Code's five-hour rate limits for Pro, Max, Team, and seat-based Enterprise plans. Second, we're removing the peak hours limit reduction on Claude Code for Pro and Max accounts. Third, we're raising our API rate limits considerably for Claude Opus models.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic also expressed interest in partnering with SpaceX to develop multiple gigawatts of orbital AI compute capacity, as compute required for next-generation systems is outpacing terrestrial power, land, and cooling.
key_facts.excerpt: As part of this agreement, we have also expressed interest in partnering with SpaceX to develop multiple gigawatts of orbital AI compute capacity.

key_facts.fact: The deal adds to Anthropic's existing compute portfolio: up to 5 GW agreement with Amazon (nearly 1 GW by end of 2026), 5 GW deal with Google and Broadcom (starting 2027), $30B Microsoft-NVIDIA Azure partnership, and $50B US AI infrastructure investment with Fluidstack.
key_facts.excerpt: An up to 5 gigawatt (GW) agreement with Amazon... a 5 GW agreement with Google and Broadcom... a strategic partnership with Microsoft and NVIDIA that includes $30 billion of Azure capacity... our $50 billion investment in American AI infrastructure with Fluidstack.

key_facts.fact: Elon Musk reversed his stance on Anthropic after spending time with senior members last week, saying 'No one set off my evil detector' — having called Anthropic 'misanthropic and evil' as recently as February.
key_facts.excerpt: In February, he declared on X that 'Anthropic hates Western Civilization'... 'I spent a lot of time last week with senior members of the Anthropic team to understand what they do to ensure Claude is good for humanity and was impressed,' Musk tweeted. 'No one set off my evil detector.'

key_facts.fact: The deal gives IPO-bound SpaceX a marquee AI customer weeks before its planned public listing targeting a $1.75T–$2T valuation, with the public S-1 expected by late May and roadshow set for the week of June 8.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX filed confidentially with the SEC on April 1 for an IPO targeting a $1.75 trillion to $2 trillion valuation, with the public S-1 expected by late May and the roadshow set for the week of June 8.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic's surging demand has been driven partly by users moving away from OpenAI after military contract controversy, increasing adoption of Claude Code in professional software development, and a shift from single-agent chat to multi-agent workflows.
key_facts.excerpt: The increase has been driven partly by users moving away from OpenAI after controversy over its agreements with the United States military, increasing adoption of Claude Code in professional software development organizations, and a user behavior (and product) shift away from single-agent, chat-based tasks.

stories.headline: China Invokes Blocking Statute for First Time, Bans Firms from Complying with US Sanctions

key_facts.fact: On May 2, China's Ministry of Commerce publicly barred companies from complying with US sanctions after the US blacklisted five Chinese refineries for processing Iranian oil — the first time China has invoked its so-called blocking statute.
key_facts.excerpt: On Saturday, China publicly barred its companies from complying with U.S. sanctions after the United States blacklisted five Chinese refineries for processing Iranian oil. This marks the first time China has invoked its so-called blocking statute—one of its strongest tools for countering foreign sanctions.

key_facts.fact: Iran's FM Abbas Araghchi met China's Wang Yi in Beijing on May 6 — his first visit since the war started on Feb 28 — to coordinate ahead of the Trump-Xi summit scheduled for May 14-15.
key_facts.excerpt: It's the Iranian envoy's first visit to China since US and Israeli strikes against his country sparked the most severe global oil supply shock in history... The meeting suggests the two sides are stepping up coordination before Trump's expected summit with Chinese leader Xi Jinping on May 14-15

key_facts.fact: Wang Yi called for a 'comprehensive ceasefire' and said China hopes relevant parties will respond to calls from the international community to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi called for a 'comprehensive ceasefire,' saying his country is deeply distressed by the war... 'The international community shares a common concern for restoring normal and safe passage through the Strait'

key_facts.fact: China accounted for up to 90% of Iran's oil exports before the war, importing over 1 million barrels per day. The blocking statute enables refiners to continue processing Iranian crude that arrives outside the US blockade area.
key_facts.excerpt: Before the war, China accounted for up to 90% of Iran's oil exports, importing over 1 million barrels each day... This enables the refiners to continue processing Iranian crude that arrives by train or is already outside the blockade area.

key_facts.fact: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said China's continued purchases of Iranian oil amounted to 'funding global terrorism.'
key_facts.excerpt: the US treasury secretary, Scott Bessent, said China's continued purchases of Iranian oil amounted to funding global terrorism.

stories.headline: Pancreatic Cancer Drug Daraxonrasib Doubles Survival in Phase 3, Results Published in NEJM

key_facts.fact: Phase 3 trial results showed patients receiving daraxonrasib plus chemotherapy had overall survival of 13.2 months vs 6.7 months for chemotherapy alone — nearly double.
key_facts.excerpt: patients who got daraxonrasib in addition to chemotherapy saw double the survival time compared with patients who just got chemotherapy... overall survival for the chemo-only group was 6.7 months, compared with 13.2 months in the combo treatment group.

key_facts.fact: Phase 1/2 results published on May 6 in the New England Journal of Medicine showed daraxonrasib stopped tumors from progressing for over 8 months and kept patients alive for up to nearly 18 months in 168 patients with advanced metastatic disease.
key_facts.excerpt: results from an earlier phase of the clinical trial were published in the New England Journal of Medicine, showing that in patients whose cancer had spread to other parts of the body, daraxonrasib stopped tumors from getting worse for more than eight months and kept patients alive for up to nearly a year and a half.

key_facts.fact: Daraxonrasib targets the RAS protein — mutated in over 90% of pancreatic cancers — long considered 'undruggable.' It works by pairing with cyclophilin A to create a 'molecular glue' that blocks RAS.
key_facts.excerpt: More than 90% of pancreatic cancers have a mutation in the gene for the RAS protein... Daraxonrasib solves the problem by pairing up with a protein called cyclophilin A inside cells. The duo work like a 'molecular glue'

key_facts.fact: The FDA has already fast-tracked the drug for approval and last week permitted drugmaker Revolution Medicines to provide it to patients outside clinical trials via an expanded access program.
key_facts.excerpt: The drug, called daraxonrasib, has already been fast-tracked for approval by the Food and Drug Administration. Last week, the agency said it would permit the drugmaker Revolution Medicines to give the drug to patients outside of clinical trials in an expanded access program.

key_facts.fact: The Phase 3 trial included patients without the KRAS mutation, suggesting potentially all pancreatic cancer patients might benefit. Only 3% of patients with metastatic disease survive five years.
key_facts.excerpt: the Phase 3 trial included patients without the KRAS mutation — suggesting potentially that all pancreatic cancer patients might benefit in some way... Just 3% of patients diagnosed with metastatic pancreatic cancer are alive five years later

stories.headline: ECB Signals Rate Hike Likely as Hormuz Crisis Pushes Eurozone Inflation to 3%, Oil Could Hit $145

key_facts.fact: ECB board member Piero Cipollone said in a May 6 speech in Milan that the chance of a rate hike has risen, stating 'the current situation seems to be drifting away from our March baseline projections, which increases the likelihood that we may need to adjust our policy rates.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'Overall, the current situation seems to be drifting away from our March baseline projections, which increases the likelihood that we may need to adjust our policy rates,' Cipollone said in a speech in Milan.

key_facts.fact: Eurozone headline inflation rose to 3% in April, driven by a 10.9% increase in energy prices, while inflation excluding energy fell to 2.2%.
key_facts.excerpt: Annual headline inflation rose to 3% in April, driven by a 10.9% increase in energy prices, whereas inflation excluding energy fell to 2.2%.

key_facts.fact: The ECB's severe scenario models oil prices peaking at $145/barrel and gas at €106/MWh in Q2 2026, which would push inflation cumulatively 6.3 percentage points higher through 2028 than December projections.
key_facts.excerpt: the severe scenario assumes an even stronger and more persistent energy price shock, with oil prices peaking at USD 145 per barrel and gas prices at €106 per MWh in the second quarter of 2026... inflation is cumulatively 6.3 percentage point higher until 2028

key_facts.fact: The net decline in global oil supply from the Iran war is estimated at around 12 million barrels per day (~11% of prewar supply), larger than the 1973, 1979, and 2022 crises combined.
key_facts.excerpt: The short-term effect of the war in Iran and the Middle East on global oil supply is larger than in the three previous energy crises (1973, 1979 and 2022) combined... the net decline in supply is estimated at around 12 million barrels per day, representing about 11% of the prewar global oil supply.

key_facts.fact: Cipollone warned Europe could start running out of jet fuel and kerosene reserves by end of May, potentially leading to restrictions 'akin to those seen during the COVID-19 pandemic.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'Europe could start running out of jet fuel and kerosene reserves by the end of May, potentially leading to material restrictions on the activity of several industries akin to those seen during the COVID-19 pandemic,' he said.

key_facts.fact: Financial markets expect three ECB rate hikes, with the first fully priced in by July. Negotiated wage growth remains at 2.6% through end-2026, suggesting workers have yet to demand compensation for the inflation surge.
key_facts.excerpt: financial markets expect three rate hikes from the ECB, with the first one fully priced in by July... Negotiated wage growth with smoothed and unsmoothed one-off payments are expected to both be 2.6% by the end of 2026

stories.headline: Google Releases Multi-Token Prediction Drafters for Gemma 4, Up to 3x Faster Inference

key_facts.fact: Google released Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) drafters for its Gemma 4 open-weight models, using speculative decoding to deliver up to 3x faster inference without any degradation in output quality or reasoning logic.
key_facts.excerpt: Google says these experimental models leverage a form of speculative decoding to take a guess at future tokens, which can speed up generation compared to the way models generate tokens on their own.

key_facts.fact: MTP drafters are smaller auxiliary models that predict several tokens at once while the main model waits for data; the main model then verifies all suggestions in a single pass, eliminating idle GPU cycles caused by memory bandwidth bottlenecks.
key_facts.excerpt: While the main model waits for its data, a small auxiliary model uses the idle capacity to suggest several tokens at once. The main model then checks all those suggestions in a single pass—if they're correct, they get accepted at once.

key_facts.fact: The speedup works across smartphones, local computers, and cloud applications; MTP drafters are available under the open Apache 2.0 license on Hugging Face and Kaggle.
key_facts.excerpt: The speedup works on smartphones, local computers, and cloud applications. The drafters are available under the open Apache 2.0 license on Hugging Face and Kaggle.

key_facts.fact: Gemma 4, introduced in early April and built on the same technology as Google's Gemini AI, has already been downloaded over 60 million times.
key_facts.excerpt: Google's Gemma 4 open-weight model, introduced in early April, has already been downloaded over 60 million times.

key_facts.fact: Google is also working to optimize Gemma 4 models of different weights for specific hardware such as Apple Silicon and NVIDIA A100 accelerators.
key_facts.excerpt: Google says it is also working to optimize Gemma 4 models of different weights for specific hardware, such as the Apple Silicon or the popular Nvidia A100.

stories.headline: Roche Agrees to Acquire PathAI for Up to $1.05B to Transform AI-Driven Diagnostics

key_facts.fact: Swiss pharmaceutical giant Roche agreed to acquire US-based PathAI, which makes AI-powered digital pathology tools, for up to $1.05 billion — $750 million upfront with up to $300 million in milestone-based payments.
key_facts.excerpt: Roche announced today that it has entered into a definitive merger agreement to acquire PathAI, a US-based company in digital pathology and AI-powered technology for pathology laboratories and the biopharma industry.

key_facts.fact: The acquisition builds on a partnership established in 2021 and expanded in 2024 to include development of AI-enabled companion diagnostic algorithms; the deal is expected to close in H2 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: This acquisition builds on the successful partnership between Roche and PathAI, established in 2021 and scaled up in 2024 to include the development of AI-enabled companion diagnostic algorithms.

key_facts.fact: PathAI's AISight Image Management System software integrates advanced AI analysis and workflow capabilities for digital pathology labs, enabling automated processing of high-resolution tissue images.
key_facts.excerpt: PathAI's AISight IMS software interface is efficient and user-friendly, seamlessly integrating advanced analysis and workflow capabilities within the digital pathology laboratory.

key_facts.fact: Roche Diagnostics CEO Matt Sause said the deal will combine PathAI's digital pathology tools with Roche's oncology diagnosis platforms to improve precision cancer diagnosis and potentially better patient outcomes.
key_facts.excerpt: 'Digital pathology has the potential to improve precision diagnosis of cancer and enable physicians to offer better tailored treatment regimens,' said Matt Sause, CEO of Roche Diagnostics.

key_facts.fact: PathAI will become part of Roche's Diagnostics division; Roche intends to scale PathAI's solutions globally and strengthen its biopharma services for precision medicine.
key_facts.excerpt: Subject to the closing of the transaction, which is expected in the second half of the year, the acquired entity will become part of the Diagnostics division.

stories.headline: Samsung Unions Threaten 18-Day Strike Starting May 21 Over AI Chip Profit Sharing

key_facts.fact: Two Samsung Electronics unions are demanding the company pay 15% of each division's operating profits to workers and raise wages by 7%. They threaten an 18-day walkout starting May 21.
key_facts.excerpt: Two Samsung unions are demanding the company pay 15 per cent of each division's operating profits to workers, as well as raise wages by 7 per cent. They have threatened an 18-day walkout starting on May 21.

key_facts.fact: Samsung management offered ~13% of operating profit to chip division staff and special rewards exceeding the OPI upper limit if DS Division achieves top position in domestic sales and profit.
key_facts.excerpt: The management proposed special rewards that would exceed the upper limit of the Outperformance Incentive (OPI) if the DS Division achieved the top position in domestic sales and operating profit.

key_facts.fact: Samsung reported record Q1 2026 results: sales of KRW 133.9T (up 69% YoY) and operating profit of KRW 57.2T (up 756%), surpassing 2025's full-year operating profit in one quarter.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Electronics reported sales of KRW 133.9 trillion, a 69% increase compared to the same period last year, and operating profit of KRW 57.2 trillion, a 756% surge. This is the highest quarterly performance ever recorded.

key_facts.fact: Samsung Vice Chairman Jeon Younghyun and President Noh Taemun urged employees not to compromise future competitiveness, warning the global business environment is challenging.
key_facts.excerpt: Vice Chairman Jeon and President Noh stated... 'In this challenging global business environment, all members of management, including ourselves, will take responsibility to ensure that we do not lose our future competitiveness.'

key_facts.fact: Board Chairman Shin Je-yoon warned a strike could cause losses of up to KRW 1T per day at semiconductor plants and reduce operating profit by up to KRW 10T if prolonged.
key_facts.excerpt: If semiconductor plant operations are halted, losses can reach tens of billions of won per minute and up to 1 trillion won per day. If the strike is prolonged, operating profit in the semiconductor division could decrease by as much as 10 trillion won.

key_facts.fact: The Bank of Korea estimates about half of Korea's Q1 GDP growth of 1.7% was attributable to chipmaking. Samsung and SK Hynix account for over 40% of the Kospi index value.
key_facts.excerpt: The Bank of Korea estimates that about half of Korea's first-quarter GDP growth of 1.7% was attributable to chipmaking. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix account for over 40% of the value of the Kospi index.

stories.headline: Scale AI Wins $500M Pentagon Contract, Five Times Its Previous $100M Deal

key_facts.fact: The Pentagon awarded Scale AI a $500 million contract to help sift through data and assist in military decision-making, a five-fold increase from its $100 million deal signed in September 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: Scale AI has won a $500m contract from the US Department of Defense, five times its previous deal... a five-fold expansion of the company's existing relationship with the department.

key_facts.fact: The contract was signed with the Pentagon's Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office (CDAO), the principal procurement vehicle for US military AI integration spending.
key_facts.excerpt: The agreement was signed with the Pentagon's Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office, the procurement vehicle driving the bulk of US military AI integration spending in 2025 and 2026.

key_facts.fact: Dan Tadross, who leads Scale AI's public sector business, said the Pentagon was 'pushing the limits' on the original contract and the deal shows the department is 'eager to adopt this technology.'
key_facts.excerpt: The Pentagon was 'pushing the limits' on the original contract, Dan Tadross, who leads Scale AI's public sector business, said in an interview. 'I think this contract is just generally proof that the department is eager to adopt this technology.'

key_facts.fact: Scale AI participates in the Defense Innovation Unit's Thunderforge programme and Trump's Golden Dome homeland defense framework, and its Scale Donovan platform deploys AI agents on networks classified up to Top Secret.
key_facts.excerpt: The company participates in the Defense Innovation Unit's Thunderforge programme... It contributes to Trump's Golden Dome homeland defense framework. Its Scale Donovan platform deploys mission-tailored AI agents on networks classified up to Top Secret.

key_facts.fact: Meta holds a 49% equity stake in Scale AI; the company developed Defense Llama, a national-security language model built on Meta's Llama 3 framework, for classified government deployment.

stories.headline: MEMS Foundry Silex Surges 127% in Stockholm IPO Debut, Strongest European Chip Listing in Five Years

key_facts.fact: Silex Microsystems debuted on Nasdaq Stockholm on May 7, with shares surging up to 127% above the IPO price of SEK 81 per share. The offering was oversubscribed several times.
key_facts.excerpt: Silex Microsystems opened sharply higher on its Nasdaq Stockholm debut on Wednesday, with the chipmaker's shares climbing in early trade after the IPO priced at SEK 81 a share. The offering had been oversubscribed several times.

key_facts.fact: The IPO raised approximately SEK 2.0B (~$220M) on a 24.6 million share offering, with a post-IPO valuation of SEK 8.9B. Proceeds split between 12.35M newly issued shares and 12.25M existing shares.
key_facts.excerpt: The deal raised approximately SEK 1.99bn ($217m) on a 24.6-million-share offering, with the equity valuation at IPO around SEK 8.9bn.

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg called it the strongest open for a sizable European IPO in almost five years. Cornerstone investors including Capital Research, Fidelity, and Swedish pension funds took ~75% of shares.
key_facts.excerpt: The debut marked the strongest open for a sizable European IPO in almost five years, after cornerstone investors took the majority of the shares in the offering.

key_facts.fact: Silex is the world's leading pure-play MEMS foundry, manufacturing micro-electromechanical systems for automotive, industrial, life sciences, and consumer electronics from a single fab near Stockholm.
key_facts.excerpt: Silex is the world's leading MEMS foundry as measured by annual revenue generated from MEMS sales in 2025. Silex operates as a pure play MEMS foundry.

key_facts.fact: Silex reported 2025 revenue of SEK 1.385B with EBIT of SEK 368M (~27% operating margin). Q1 2026 was stronger: SEK 375M revenue and SEK 128M EBIT (~34% operating margin).
key_facts.excerpt: Net sales for the year ended 31 December 2025 reached SEK 1,385m, with EBIT of SEK 368m, an operating margin around 27 per cent. First-quarter 2026 numbers were stronger still, with SEK 375m of revenue and SEK 128m of EBIT.

key_facts.fact: Silex's Chinese shareholder Sai MicroElectronics sold existing shares as part of the offering. The IPO welcomed 14,000 new shareholders.

stories.headline: Anthropic Signs Deal for All of SpaceX's Colossus 1: 220,000+ NVIDIA GPUs and 300MW of Capacity

key_facts.fact: Anthropic signed a deal to use all compute capacity at SpaceX's Colossus 1 data center in Memphis, gaining access to 220,000+ NVIDIA GPUs (H100, H200, GB200) and 300MW of new capacity within the month.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic on Wednesday announced a deal with Elon Musk's SpaceX to use all of the compute capacity at his company's Colossus 1 data center in Memphis, Tennessee... more than 300 megawatts of compute capacity.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic also expressed interest in partnering with SpaceX to develop multiple gigawatts of orbital AI compute capacity, citing terrestrial power, land, and cooling constraints.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic also 'expressed interest' in working with SpaceX to develop multiple gigawatts of compute capacity in space.

key_facts.fact: Musk reversed his stance on Anthropic, saying he spent time with their team and was 'impressed.' In February he had called Anthropic 'misanthropic' and said Claude 'hates Western Civilization.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'Everyone I met was highly competent and cared a great deal about doing the right thing. No one set off my evil detector,' Musk wrote. 'Anthropic hates Western Civilization,' Musk wrote in February.

key_facts.fact: Musk confirmed xAI 'will be dissolved as a separate company' and will be called SpaceXAI. SpaceX has moved its AI training to Colossus 2.
key_facts.excerpt: In a separate post on X on Wednesday, Musk said that xAI 'will be dissolved as a separate company' and will be called SpaceXAI.

key_facts.fact: The deal adds to Anthropic's growing stack of compute agreements: up to 5GW with Amazon, 5GW with Google/Broadcom, $30B Azure capacity with Microsoft/Nvidia, and $50B US AI infra with Fluidstack.

key_facts.fact: Reports have highlighted that xAI was only utilizing ~11% of its installed compute resources due to unoptimized software stacks, freeing capacity for the Anthropic lease.

stories.headline: UN Security Council Holds Emergency Session After Iran Launches 12 Ballistic Missiles at UAE

key_facts.fact: The UN Security Council held a closed-door meeting on May 6 focused on Iranian missile and drone attacks on the UAE on Monday, briefed by Under-Secretary-General Rosemary DiCarlo.
key_facts.excerpt: the Under-Secretary-General for Political and Peacebuilding Affairs, Rosemary DiCarlo, briefed a closed-door Security Council meeting focused on the missile and drone attacks on the United Arab Emirates (UAE) on Monday.

key_facts.fact: The UAE Ambassador said Iran launched 12 ballistic missiles, 3 cruise missiles, and 4 UAVs at the UAE, striking the Fujairah oil industry zone and injuring 3 civilians. Most threats were intercepted by UAE air defenses.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran launched 12 ballistic missiles, three cruise missiles and four UAVs (unmanned aerial vehicles, or drones) which resulted in a fire in the Fujairah oil industry zone that affected critical civilian energy infrastructure... three civilians were injured

key_facts.fact: Since the crisis began on February 28, the UAE has intercepted over 500 ballistic missiles, nearly 30 cruise missiles, and more than 2,000 UAVs launched from Iran.
key_facts.excerpt: the UAE 'has intercepted over 500 ballistic missiles, nearly 30 cruise missiles and more than 2,000 UAVs launched from Iran' since 28 February

key_facts.fact: The International Maritime Organization confirmed 32 maritime incidents and 10 fatalities to date, including an attack on French vessel San Antonio on May 5 that injured 8 seafarers.
key_facts.excerpt: the International Maritime Organization(IOM) confirmed an attack on a French vessel, the San Antonio, in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday which injured eight seafarers. The agency has confirmed 32 incidents and 10 fatalities to date.

key_facts.fact: The emergency session was requested by Bahrain, which called the attacks a 'clear violation' of Security Council resolution 2817 (2026) adopted in March after Iranian attacks on neighboring countries.

stories.headline: US and Iran Close In on 14-Point MOU to End War; Iran Expected to Reply Thursday

key_facts.fact: The US presented a one-page, 14-point memorandum of understanding to Iran that would declare an end to the war and trigger a 30-day negotiation period on nuclear issues, unfreezing assets, and Hormuz security.
key_facts.excerpt: Axios describes the memorandum as a one-page, 14-point memo which could set a framework for more detailed nuclear negotiations. Among the provisions it lists are a suspension on Iranian nuclear enrichment, the lifting of sanctions, and restoring free transit through the Strait of Hormuz.

key_facts.fact: Iran is expected to give mediators its reply to the proposal on Thursday, according to a regional source.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran is expected to give mediators its reply to the proposal Thursday, a regional source told CNN.

key_facts.fact: The MOU includes discussion of a moratorium on uranium enrichment for longer than 10 years and requires Iran to ship its stockpile of highly enriched uranium out of the country.
key_facts.excerpt: the source familiar said it would include discussion of a moratorium on uranium enrichment for a period of longer than 10 years... The plan also requires Iran to ship its stockpile of highly enriched uranium out of the country.

key_facts.fact: Trump said the US has had 'very good talks with Iran in the last 24 hours' and that a deal is possible, but also threatened that if Iran doesn't agree, 'the bombing starts' at 'a much higher level and intensity.'
key_facts.excerpt: the president said the US has had 'very good talks with Iran in the last 24 hours' and that was deal is possible... he also issued a new threat to Iran, writing on Truth Social that if Tehran doesn't come to an agreement, the 'bombing starts'

key_facts.fact: US Central Command shot at and disabled an Iranian-flagged oil tanker M/T Hasna in the Gulf of Oman on May 6 after it attempted to violate the US blockade, using 20mm cannon fire from an F/A-18 Super Hornet launched from USS Abraham Lincoln.
key_facts.excerpt: U.S. forces disabled the tanker's rudder by firing several rounds from the 20mm cannon gun of a U.S. Navy F/A-18 Super Hornet launched from USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN 72). Hasna is no longer transiting to Iran.

key_facts.fact: Iranian foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said the US proposal 'is still being reviewed by Iran' and after finalizing its viewpoints, Iran will convey them to the Pakistani mediators.
key_facts.excerpt: Iranian foreign ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei told the Iranian Students' News Agency (ISNA): 'The American proposal is still being reviewed by Iran and after concluding, it will inform the Pakistani side of its opinion.'

key_facts.fact: A senior member of Iran's parliament dismissed the proposal as a 'wish list' and said Iran 'has its finger on the trigger and is ready' to deliver a 'harsh response' if the US does not 'surrender.'
key_facts.excerpt: Ebrahim Rezaei, the spokesperson of the Iranian Parliament's national security and foreign policy commission, wrote on X: 'The Americans will not gain anything in a war they are losing'... He also said Iran 'has its finger on the trigger and is ready'
